correctness.rationale: For K_R defined by x²+y²<=R², x²+z²<=R², y²+z²<=R², its ray gauge is rho_K(u)=R/sqrt(1-min_i u_i²) because each cylinder bounds r²(1-u_i²). Hence any central plane H_n has exact area R²/2 ∫_{unit great circle} (1-min u_i²)^-1 dθ, with integrand uniformly <=3/2. Six pair-equality planes ui=±uj meet generic H_n in twelve oriented rays; each sector has constant minimizing coordinate ell. Orthogonal projection omitting ell maps this sector to a radius-R circular sector and has area Jacobian |n_ell|, giving twelve atan2(kΔ,D)/(2k) contributions. Continuity by dominated convergence handles exceptional normals. Integrand >=1 proves A>=πR², equality requiring whole great circle lie in union of coordinate zero circles, forcing a coordinate plane. Independent 240k-angle midpoint polar quadrature gives A(e3)=π, A((1,1,0)/√2)=3.63565503163=√2(1+π/2), A((1,1,1)/√3)=3.34372984533=6√3 atan(1/3), and a generic normal 3.41350487818. Near n=(δp,δq,sqrt(1-δ²)), u3² yields π δ² before subtracting four coordinate-node neighborhoods: positive-part integrals of (δ²p²-s²)_+ and (δ²q²-s²)_+ give cubic correction -4/3(|p|³+|q|³)δ³ with uniform O(δ⁴). Independent quadrature at δ=.04,.02,.01 for axial and equal-component p,q yielded cubic estimates tending to -1.333333 and -0.942809. The even non-polynomial |p|³+|q|³ term prevents degree-3 Taylor polynomial.
residual_risks: Numerical polar integrations corroborate selected normals, not the all-normal twelve-sector formula or uniform asymptotic; rigorous proof uses branch partition, projected sector Jacobian and uniform local node control.

value.rationale: The Steinmetz tricylinder is a classical natural body. An exact all-normal central-section area law, sharp minimizer set, and non-polynomial cubic angular response near minimizers provide a useful integral-geometric invariant beyond known volumes. Its finite 12-sector complexity is geometrically forced by equal-coordinate active-constraint boundaries, not an arbitrary enumeration.
